title: Best Served Cold
author: Abercrombie, Joe
review:
4.5/5

This is my favorite Abercrombie book so far. He excels when the stories are smaller and the stakes are lower. The First Law trilogy really struggled trying to fill the boots of epic fantasy, this one doesn't try to do that and it results in a better story that's more focused in what it wants to accomplish.

The dialogue in this book is amazing and sharply written, there's a lot of laugh out loud moments and the characters jump out of the page and are well defined. You can often tell what character is talking based on just how they're talking which is really impressive. The characters are really well developed and complex here, the world is very gray and often completely black where everyone is sort of awful all the time, but there are some moments of friendship; before they turn around and try to kill each-other that is.

This is one of the best audiobooks I've ever listened to. Steven Pacey deserves heaps of praise, every character sounds unique and he brings the story to life as a play performed by one man. I have no idea how he pulls it off but he often goes from one character to another mid-breath and even in certain moments has characters pretending to be other characters...just amazing.
